title: Altermagnetic memcapacitors
abstract: We propose a spintronic memcapacitance effect based upon altermagnetic multiferroic materials. We identify the rare-earth vanadates RVO$_3$ as a concrete platform, with all key parameters tied to measured properties. Under an oscillating electric field, the resulting charge and spin currents trace pinched hysteresis loops that close tangentially at zero field -- the hallmark of memcapacitive, type-2 memdevice behavior -- with charge current densities exceeding, by a factor of about 3.6, the lowest deterministic switching current density reported for optimized spin-transfer-torque magnetic tunnel junctions. We model the system theoretically as a dimerized two-orbital $d$-wave altermagnetic lattice via a Su--Schrieffer--Heeger-type bond modulation, in the spirit of the spin-dependent Rice--Mele model, thereby coupling the altermagnetic order to field-switchable charge and spin polarizations. The associated polarization loops close tangentially at zero field and yield a sign-changing, history-dependent ``butterfly'' differential capacitance, identifying the device as a genuine memcapacitor. Both responses are protected by the same inversion symmetry, so charge and spin channels switch simultaneously with no separate control needed. These results establish altermagnetic multiferroics, realized concretely in RVO$_3$, as an efficient, non-volatile platform for combined electric and spintronic memory.
summary: This paper proposes using altermagnetic multiferroics, specifically RVO3, as a highly efficient platform for combined electric and spintronic memory. By modeling the system with a dimerized lattice Hamiltonian, the authors predict a unique memcapacitive response characterized by a "butterfly" capacitance loop. This work establishes a fundamental link between altermagnetic order and non-volatile, electrically switchable charge/spin storage.
main_problem: To establish a theoretical and experimental platform for combined electric and spintronic memory using altermagnetic multiferroic materials.
main_result: Altermagnetic multiferroics in RVO3 are shown to be an efficient, non-volatile platform for combined electric and spintronic memory, exhibiting a genuine memcapacitive response.
method: The system is modeled using a dimerized two-orbital d-wave altermagnetic lattice Hamiltonian, analyzed via mean-field theory to derive coupled charge and spin polarization currents.
model_or_system: The physical system is rare-earth vanadates (RVO3), modeled as a dimerized altermagnetic lattice. The Hamiltonian couples hopping terms, Heisenberg spin exchange, and orbital exchange, modulated by a dimerization parameter $\delta$.
key_observables: Memcapacitance (butterfly differential capacitance), pinched hysteretic charge/spin current-field loops, and simultaneous switching of charge and spin polarizations.
important_parameters: Dimerization parameter $\delta$, external electric field $E_y$, and the coupling strength between altermagnetism and polarization.
main_assumptions: The coupling between charge and spin is protected by the same inversion symmetry, ensuring simultaneous switching; the model is anchored to the orbital-Peierls transition in RVO3.
figures_summary: Figure 4 shows polarization loops closing tangentially at the origin and a sign-changing, two-branch "butterfly" differential capacitance loop, confirming memcapacitive behavior.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical problem and platform (RVO3) to developing the theoretical model (Hamiltonian, mean-field theory) and finally demonstrating the key diagnostic signatures (memcapacitance loops) that validate its use as a memory element.
why_interesting: The work demonstrates a mechanism where intrinsic magnetic order (altermagnetism) dictates the electrical switching behavior, providing a novel, symmetry-protected route to coupled charge/spin memory that is highly relevant to advanced condensed matter device physics.
